newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RALLYING-SAINZ LEADS AFTER MCRAE SUFFERS BROKEN CAMSHAFT.
newsitem.headline: RALLYING-SAINZ LEADS AFTER MCRAE SUFFERS BROKEN CAMSHAFT.

text.p: Carlos Sainz of Spain ended the first leg of the New Zealand rally with a narrow 22-second lead over Sweden's Kenneth Eriksson after Briton Colin McRae had retired on Sunday.

Sainz, driving a Ford Escort, took advantage and control of the rally when the luckless McRae, in a Subaru, suffered a broken camshaft belt two-thirds of the way through the ninth of the day's 10 stages.
McRae had led the rally from the start and had built up a lead of 57 seconds before being forced out of the event he has won three times in recent years.

It was a particularly galling blow because McRae's world championship rival, current leader and defending champion Tommi Makinen of Finland, had rolled his Mitsubishi Lancer car on stage four and retired earlier in the day.

After the opening leg, run on mainly gravel stages in cloudy and overcast conditions on the forest roads in the narrow peninsula to the north of New Zealand's largest city, Sainz looked capable of repeating his success at the previous rally, in Greece, two months ago.

He finished the day at the overnight halt at Manukau with an overall time of one minute and 26.14 seconds. Eriksson was second in his Subaru Impreza 22 seconds behind and four-times world champion Juha Kankunnen of Finland third in another Ford Escort.
Richard Burns of Britain, who won the rally when it was a non-championship event least year, was fourth at the end of the day in his Mitsubishi Carisma, two minutes and nine seconds behind Sainz.
